cues: The proximal tubule takes back all the glucose and amino acids and most of the salt and water.
The descending limb lets water out; the ascending limb pumps salt out but will not let water follow.
The distal tubule and collecting duct fine tune, under the control of hormones.
Step three, secretion: the tubule adds hydrogen ions, potassium, creatinine and drugs, which is how the kidney controls blood pH.
text: Step two: selective reabsorption. The proximal tubule takes back all the glucose and amino acids and most of the salt and water. The descending limb lets water out; the ascending limb pumps salt out but will not let water follow. The distal tubule and collecting duct fine tune, under the control of hormones. Step three, secretion: the tubule adds hydrogen ions, potassium, creatinine and drugs, which is how the kidney controls blood pH.
